content.context: Three existing records also turned out to be corrupt: two written by pitmry-antigravity-bridge with stale content hashes, one carrying a foreign source_artifact shape with no original_text or source_hash. An external bridge writing straight into .pitmry/records/ bypasses PITMRY validation entirely, and it will do so again unless the bridge is fixed or the store refuses foreign shapes. Separately, the working tree already held an unrelated uncommitted pass removing hardcoded stat-tile sparklines and rewording tile copy; it was committed alongside this work because splitting mid-file was not practical.
content.decision: Correctness gates features. The user sequenced the conflict fix before any additional panel fields, on the grounds that more fields on a resolver that cannot flag contradictions makes the panel more confident and less correct. Every later choice followed that rule: the panel reads peers from the resolver rather than re-deriving them, trust and progress are reported as separate axes, lifecycle bookkeeping is kept canonical but made unretrievable, repair never invents history, and grouping is proved lossless by a check script.
content.rationale: Three failures shared one shape: a component reported success it had not verified. The resolver reported OK while contradicting claims stood unresolved. The dashboard reported a state it could not substantiate. The projection reported a healthy store while answering NO_MATCH. In a tool whose premise is that memory can be trusted, a confident wrong answer costs more than an absent one, so each fix was to make the system able to say 'I do not know' rather than to add surface area.
